test_title: SSC CGL 2024 Tier-II Official Paper-I (Held On: 18 Jan, 2025)
subject: general
question: Which statement accurately describes vascular plants based on the information in the passage?

options.text: Vascular plants lack stems, roots and leaves.
Vascular plants are unicellular in structure.
Vascular plants have true stems, roots and leaves, unlike algae.
Algae and vascular plants share the same morphoanatomical characteristics.

solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The passage draws a clear structural distinction between algae and vascular plants. It states that **algae "do not... have the actual stems, roots or leaves found in vascular plants."**
 
• By logic, this means that **vascular plants possess true stems, roots, and leaves**, which serves as a defining difference between the two groups.
 
• The text also mentions that algae lack other "morphoanatomical characteristics typical of vascular plants," highlighting that vascular plants have a more complex anatomy.
 
• **Option 3** is the only choice that correctly identifies this contrast based on the text provided.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

**Correct Sentence from Text:** *"They [Algae] do not, however, have the **actual stems, roots or leaves found in vascular plants**."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1:** Incorrect. The passage explicitly states that these structures are "found in vascular plants."
 
• **Option 2:** Incorrect. The passage mentions **algae** can be unicellular, but it does not attribute this trait to vascular plants.
 
• **Option 4:** Incorrect. The passage states that algae **"do not have"** the morphoanatomical characteristics typical of vascular plants.
